title: Assurance OKR mapping and milestone dependency graph for compliance releases
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Objective: produce a living milestone dependency graph that maps Assurance OKRs (SOC2, ISO27001, SSO/audit-log deliverables) to sprint milestones, engineering tickets, and artifact ownership. This ticket covers the PM deliverables: taxonomy, OKR->milestone mapping, acceptance criteria, implementation plan for an evidence collection pipeline, and rollout playbook for cross-functional stakeholders (Eng, Security, Design, Support).

Scope: define schema for milestones and evidence types, instrument a lightweight graph representation (DAG) in Confluence + maintainable JSON export, feed the graph to a dashboard for Release Readiness and risk heatmaps, and define automation touchpoints for ENG to populate evidence status via PR tags and CI checks. Excludes: full implementation of backend evidence storage (tracked in ENG dependencies).

Success criteria: 1) OKRs and milestones are traceable in the graph with owners for 90% of SOC2/ISO required artifacts; 2) Dashboard shows red/amber/green readiness per milestone updated by ENG inputs; 3) Runbook for release gating and escalation is published and has PM+Security signoff; 4) Evidence collection automation triage plan is agreed and assigned to ENG backlog.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence graph page created with interactive DAG and legend
JSON export format documented and validated against ENG-4021 API contract
Mapping table that links each OKR to specific milestone keys and ENG/SP tasks completed
Runbook for release gating published and shared with stakeholders
Kickoff plan for evidence-collector sprint (ENG backlog) with owners and estimates
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: ENG bandwidth to implement automation is limited -> Mitigation: prioritize manual upload path for critical artifacts and schedule automation as follow-up (low-lift CI checks first)
Risk: inconsistent artifact naming across teams -> Mitigation: enforce minimal artifact schema and provide naming templates and pre-commit checks
Risk: sensitive evidence in Drive/KMS -> Mitigation: require S3/KMS-backed storage and redact PII; Security to review storage pattern before rollout
